articles.title: Plans for Demolition of Flats in Lower Falinge Resurface
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has revealed plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, sparking distress among remaining residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has announced plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge, which contain 126 homes, as part of a redevelopment project. The proposed plans aim to replace the existing flats with 270 new homes, including a mix of flats and houses, situated between St Mary’s Gate and Sheriff Street.

The maisonette blocks known as Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, and Vaynor are all set for demolition. Only the Zedburgh block, which is currently occupied, remains. Andy Roche, a resident of the Zedburgh block since 1988, expressed his distress over the news, stating that both he and his partner are struggling with the prospect of eviction.

RBH previously faced a legal challenge that halted demolition plans last year, but the new proposals have now been revealed. Roche claims that the housing association has not adequately listened to the residents' concerns. He stated, "I don’t believe they have listened to the residents of the estate at all," highlighting the emotional toll the situation has taken on him and his partner, both of whom are autistic.

RBH has stated that the blocks are no longer fit for purpose and have exceeded their lifespan. The estate has seen previous redevelopment efforts, with 100 new homes already built following earlier demolition work. The latest plans have been informed by consultations with local residents, according to RBH.
